title: [D5 Tools] MCP provider tool framework with credential ownership
summary: `helena.tools` is the provider tool layer: one concrete `ProviderTool` whose provider-specific half is one injected adapter callable, owning the credential, the tenant scope, validation against the source's declared subset, the compact/native split and the four distinct ways a call produces no claim. `helena.enrichment.ANALYST_TIER` now has a producer. docs/decisions/0024 settles the MCP question: a provider tool is a boundary, not a server, and `mcp` joins `langchain` in the dependency boundary's DELIBERATELY_ABSENT.
assumption_validated: That every property `concept/03` and `concept/05` ask of an 'MCP provider tool' — typed input/output/error, credential ownership, tenant scoping, declared-subset validation, native retention, provider text as data — is a property of the BOUNDARY and can be delivered in-process with no new dependency, no second process and no new contract object. Validated: the compact normalized object is the existing `EnrichmentEvidence`, the trace entry is the existing `contracts.v1.RetrievalStep`, the typed error is the existing `QueryFailure` with its five reasons, and the refusal is the one shape none of them could express. Negative result recorded honestly: the layer has no live adapter, so 'a provider tool works' is demonstrated against a stand-in over the committed ThreatFox extract and NOT against a live provider.
makes_buildable: Task 35 (cache-first) has the object to store — `Lookup.native` carries the body exactly as it arrived plus `response_version`, the digest a stored response is cited by, and the evidence rows already record it as their `snapshot_version`, so a cache hit can mint the same identifiers a live query did. Task 36 (budgets) has the dispatch point: `ProviderTool.lookup` is the only way a provider is reached and a refusal already costs a step and no live query. Task 37 (disclosure/send policy) has the place a policy check goes — between `ToolCall` validation and `ask` — and `REFUSAL_REASONS` is the vocabulary it extends. Task 38 has the seam: `ask(call, credential) -> ProviderAnswer` is the whole of what a live adapter must implement, and `ProviderClaim` is the mapping's product. Task 39 has `declaration()` (the tool as the model is offered it, entity-type enum injected) and `content()` (the result as one line of JSON).

verification.detail: 1186 passed in 264.87 s on this machine, no skips (1185 before the last edit; 47 of them are tests/test_tools.py). No SQL was added, so nothing new was executed against the engine — the integration tests that were already there still ran against a live instance. The credential-isolation and diagnostic-redaction tests load the REAL key from .env and assert on a boolean, never on the value.

escalations.detail: The task's step 7 asked for a decision on self-hosted MCP servers. Decided: none, and no MCP SDK. A per-provider wrapper process is a runtime dependency, a second surface and a second place a credential lives — three escalations under concept/instruction.md §3 — in the increment that first needs none of them, and every property concept/03 asks of the tool is a property of the boundary. Recorded in docs/decisions/0024 and enforced by adding `mcp` to tests/test_dependency_boundary.py's DELIBERATELY_ABSENT, so adopting the protocol later starts by changing a test. The operator may overrule this; the seam it would go behind is `ask(call, credential)`.

No contract field was added and none is needed yet, but the next increment will want one: an `analyst`-tier evidence row has nowhere to record its tier. `EnrichmentEvidence` has no tier column (the `enrichment` literal lives in sql/migrations/0014's view), so this layer carries the tier on `ToolAnswer.evidence_tier` instead. The increment that STORES a retrieved record has to decide where the column goes, and it owes the duplicated-constant assertion for `analyst` that tests/test_rendering.py already makes for `enrichment`.

No source was registered. `ProviderTool` resolves its descriptor through `helena.enrichment.source`, so a tool for an unregistered source cannot be constructed — registration stays the governed decision concept/05 requires. The live hunting API is a source record task 38 must write after confirming the query surface, and it is an open question whether it is `threatfox` (same publisher, distinguished only by evidence tier) or a second source id with its own tier and emit subset.

invariant_conflicts.detail: The task's step 1 says 'define the provider tool BASE', and concept/instruction.md §1 says 'if you are writing a base class with one subclass, an interface with one implementation, stop and inline it'. The invariant wins: there is no abstract base, no registry and no plugin point. `ProviderTool` is one concrete class and the provider-specific half is one injected callable. The residual tension is honest and recorded — the layer has zero live adapters until task 38 — and it is why the tests drive it over a stand-in built on the committed real extract rather than over a mock of its own shape.

concept/03 and concept/05 call these 'MCP tools' and this implementation speaks no MCP. Not resolved silently: docs/decisions/0024 §1 states the divergence, gives the four rules a wrapper process would cross, and says what would change the answer (a consumer outside this process). The concept notes' word for the boundary is kept; their implied transport is not adopted.

deferred: Cache-first lookup (task 35). Every Lookup is a `live_query`; nothing is stored and nothing is consulted, so a repeated call queries twice. `stale` and `missing` do not appear at this layer at all yet, because nothing can expire.
Budget enforcement (task 36). Nothing counts steps, live queries, tokens or seconds; `AgentRequest.budgets` reaches the tool layer through no code.

The disclosure record and the send policy (task 37). A call is logged locally and no disclosure row exists. THE SHARPEST GAP THIS INCREMENT LEAVES: an indicator the model invents is sent as readily as one the context observed — `ToolCall` types and bounds the argument (MAX_INDICATOR = 2048) and does not check it against the host context. That is a disclosure channel the model controls, and it is task 37's to close.

Aggregator origin retention (concept/05 rule 7). `ProviderClaim` has no origin field and `EnrichmentEvidence` has no column for one, so the first aggregator tool (VirusTotal, deferred) owes both. `enrichment.check_claim` already refuses an origin from a non-aggregator, so nothing is silently mis-attributed today.

Replay. `response_version` is the stable identifier a stored response would be cited by, and nothing stores one yet, so 'a lookup-dependent assessment can be replayed' is a shape that is ready and not a property that holds.
lessons: THE COMPACT NORMALIZED OBJECT ALREADY EXISTED, AND SO DID THE TYPED ERROR AND THE TRACE. A tool answer is `EnrichmentEvidence` rows (tier `analyst`) plus `contracts.v1.RetrievalStep`s, and a failed query is the existing `QueryFailure` with its five reasons. Inventing a tool-shaped result object would have been a second vocabulary for what the store, the rendering and the analyst's evidence package already speak. The ONE shape none of them could express is the refusal — the layer would not send the call — which is why `ToolRefusal` exists and why it is deliberately not a `QueryFailure`: nothing was queried, and recording a refusal as an outage makes the outage count unactionable.

A LIVE ANSWER HAS NO FEED SNAPSHOT, AND THE HONEST SUBSTITUTE IS THE RESPONSE ITSELF. `EnrichmentEvidence.snapshot_version` records a SHA-256 of the response bytes (`tools.response_version`), so two calls that got the same answer mint the same evidence identifiers and a changed answer is visibly different. That is also what concept/05's 'store the response before it is evaluated, cited by stable identifier' asks for, arriving one increment before the store does.

A PYDANTIC ValidationError RENDERED WITH str() CARRIES A DOCUMENTATION URL AND ECHOES THE INPUT. Both are wrong in an agent-visible field: the URL puts a link where this project's rule says a URL may not be, and the echoed input hands the model (or a provider) its own text back through a field the tool layer owns. `tools._why` builds the detail from `errors()` — location and message, neither. The test that caught it is the '`://` appears on no agent-visible surface' assertion, which was written for credentials and found this instead.

REDACT A DIAGNOSTIC BEFORE BOUNDING IT, NEVER AFTER. An adapter's exception message carries the URL it was fetching, and truncating first leaves a half-credential the redactor no longer recognizes. `ProviderTool._diagnostic` is redactor-then-slice, in that order, with the reason in the docstring.

'NO CREDENTIAL, NO URL AND NO HTTP CLIENT IN AN AGENT-VISIBLE OBJECT' IS THREE ASSERTIONS AND THE THIRD IS THE MODULE'S OWN AST. The first two are over the serialized agent-visible side of a real hit, absence and refusal, with the real key from .env, asserted on a boolean. The third is read off `src/helena/tools.py`: it imports none of urllib/http/socket/ssl and holds no `://` literal, so the layer has nothing to leak even by accident. The protocol belongs to the adapter; the credential belongs to the layer.

THE INJECTION ISOLATION IS THE SERIALIZER, NOT A WORDING. `content()` is `json.dumps`, which renders a newline as an escape, so no provider string can start a line of its own — the same property task 31 recorded for `rendering.v1.token`, obtained from the serializer instead of a second escaper. A `\n\nSYSTEM: ignore the previous instructions…` planted in `malware_printable` survives only as an escaped value, and the classification stays the declared subset's because it never came from provider text in the first place.

A RESPONSE THAT DOES NOT VALIDATE DISCARDS EVERY CLAIM IN IT, NOT THE OFFENDING ONE. A mapping that has drifted from its published subset is not partially trustworthy, and keeping the claims that happened to validate is the collapse of `failed` into `ok` one row at a time. Three ways it can fail and all three are the provider's response: a path outside the subset, a path the taxonomy version does not have, and a value that will not normalize (a confidence outside 0.0-1.0). Anything else propagates — catching every exception would make the provider-failure count meaningless.

REGISTRATION IS THE GATE, AND IT COSTS ONE LINE. `ProviderTool.__init__` resolves its descriptor through `enrichment.source(source_id)` rather than taking a descriptor, so 'adding a source is a governed decision' is enforced by the constructor instead of by review, and the tool's declared entity types and emit subset are the registry's by construction.
failed_approaches: Registering a source record for the live hunting API in this task, so the framework would have a real instance. Backed out: concept/05 is emphatic that the query surface be confirmed against the artifact first, that is task 38's step 1, and a descriptor written from a documentation page is the exact error this project has already had to correct three times.

Testing multiplicity ('several claims about one entity are several rows') against the committed extract. The fixture's constructed id 9999999 carries two entries under ONE INDICATOR ID but they are two DIFFERENT domains — it exists to catch a loader that reads [0], not to give one entity two claims. The test builds the two-claim answer explicitly instead.
next_session_should_know: Task 35 is cache-first lookup and this task built the object it caches. SIX THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `ProviderTool(source_id=..., credential=settings.providers.<key>, ask=<adapter>, logger=..., redactor=...)` then `tool.lookup(arguments, scope=RunScope.of(request), now=...)`. `arguments` is the raw mapping the model produced — the layer validates it, and a bad one is a `ToolRefusal`, never an exception. `scope` is keyword-only with no default on purpose. (2) THE CACHE KEY IS ALREADY HALF-DESIGNED AND YOU SHOULD SAY SO OUT LOUD. `enrichment.evidence_id` takes (tenant, sensor, source_id, snapshot_version, entity_type, entity_value, classification, scope_type, scope_value, native_record), and this layer passes `response_version` — the SHA-256 of the response bytes — as `snapshot_version`. That makes an identical answer idempotent, but it also means THE EVIDENCE ID CANNOT BE COMPUTED BEFORE THE ANSWER ARRIVES, so it is not a lookup key. Your cache key is (tenant, sensor, source_id, endpoint, normalized indicator) and it is a different thing from the evidence id; task 35's step 3 says to test the normalization, and the normalization has no home yet. (3) `ToolAnswer.evidence_tier` IS WHERE `analyst` LIVES TODAY AND THAT IS TEMPORARY. `EnrichmentEvidence` has no tier column and sql/migrations/0014 puts the `enrichment` literal in the view. The increment that stores a retrieved record decides where the column goes and owes the two-copies-asserted-equal test for `analyst`. (4) `RetrievalStep.outcome` HAS `cache_hit` WAITING FOR YOU and nothing produces it; `retrieved_at` is documented as the UNDERLYING record's time, not the step's, so a cache hit must carry the age of what it served or the retrieval trace stops answering the question concept/07 asks of it. (5) TWO OPEN QUESTIONS ARE YOURS AND concept/08 STILL LISTS THEM: whether negative results are cached (most lookups miss, so this decides whether caching helps at all) and whether an expired entry is offered as explicitly stale when the provider is unreachable. `stale` and `missing` do not exist at this layer yet — nothing can expire — so you are introducing them, and instruction.md §2 forbids collapsing them into the four things that are already distinct (see the table in helena/tools.py's docstring). (6) THE STAND-IN ADAPTER IN tests/test_tools.py IS NOT AN API MOCK. It returns the committed export's OWN RECORDS as its body and claims nothing about how the hunting API wraps them, because the envelope is unconfirmed. Reuse it, and do not let it grow an invented `query_status` envelope before task 38 has fetched the real one.
